answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through geomagnetic attestation. Nodes authenticate by submitting cryptographic proofs of localized magnetic fluctuations measured near ferrous ground deposits, spanning from arctic tundra to umber bedrock. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware and logistics cost of deploying physically separated sensor probes per identity. However, solar flare activity can distort ambient magnetic fields, triggering false-positive rejections of legitimate agents.
